title: Word tally (synthetic)
audience: Writers who want a quick count from the command line (synthetic).
problem_statement:
Writers paste text into web pages to count words, which is slow and sends drafts to a third party.
A local command would count without the text leaving the computer.

user_flows.name: Count lines
steps: Pipe text into the command with --lines

scope: Count whitespace-separated words read from standard input
Count non-empty lines with the --lines option
Refuse an unknown option with exit code 2 and no output
non_goals: No reading from files or folders

data_contracts.name: standard input
data_contracts.description: UTF-8 text typed or piped by the user; made-up in tests.

acceptance_checks.statement: The number of whitespace-separated words is printed.
acceptance_checks.measure: Standard output is the count and a line end; exit code 0. An unknown option gives no output and exit code 2.

acceptance_checks.statement: With --lines, the number of non-empty lines is printed.
acceptance_checks.measure: Standard output is the count and a line end; exit code 0.

acceptance_checks.statement: The program does nothing the scope does not list.
acceptance_checks.measure: A reviewer reads the source and finds no reading or writing of files and no network use. Finding the program’s own folder to import its modules does not count as file use.

risks.risk: Counts differ from a writer’s word processor
risks.mitigation: The README states how words are counted and how lines are counted, in one sentence each.

obligations: Re-run the checks after any change

tasks.title: Count words from standard input
tasks.deliverable: src/main.py prints the word count and refuses unknown options.

tasks.title: Add the --lines option
tasks.deliverable: src/main.py accepts --lines and prints the line count.

tasks.title: Review against the scope
tasks.deliverable: A written review of the source against the scope.
